title: Storage is pluggable
description:
As an app embedding Virtuus (Swift, wasm, tests), I want tables on any storage backend, so that the engine doesn't assume a filesystem.

```gherkin
Feature: Pluggable storage
  Scenario: A table on memory storage works without touching the disk
    Given a table "notes" with primary key "id" on memory storage
    When I put {"id": "n1", "text": "hi"} into "notes"
    Then getting "n1" from "notes" returns {"id": "n1", "text": "hi"}
    And no files were written to disk

  Scenario: Writes to file storage are atomic
    Given a table "notes" with primary key "id" on file storage in a temporary directory
    When I put 100 records into "notes"
    Then the table directory holds exactly 100 ".json" files and no temporary files
```
